archetypes.name: phase-contract
archetypes.rationale: The plan adds a phase driver and result-env handoff, so it needs focused review against existing driver contracts and wrapper expectations.
archetypes.prompt_body: Compare the proposed design-publish.sh contract against the existing phase-driver conventions, sibling scripts, and SKILL.md handoff semantics. Look for mismatches in argv validation, exit codes, result-env keys, stdout fallback behavior, quiet-stream expectations, and whether the orchestrator can reliably distinguish plan-write failure from configuration errors. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: publish-ordering
archetypes.rationale: The extraction is mostly about preserving mutation ordering and skip gates, making sequencing defects the highest-value specialist angle.
archetypes.prompt_body: Audit whether the plan fully preserves the current Step 5c mutation order and skip conditions while moving logic from prose into design-publish.sh. Focus on GitHub-affecting operations, reentry marker placement, plan-block-write failure behavior, SESSION_ID and PUBLISH_OK rename gating, diagram upsert non-blocking behavior, and final-summary render timing. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.

archetypes.name: drift-harness
archetypes.rationale: The plan relocates behavior from SKILL prose into scripts, so stale structural pins and documentation drift are likely failure modes.
archetypes.prompt_body: Check whether the proposed harness, script-md sibling docs, Makefile target registration, and structural grep updates are sufficient to prevent contract drift after the Step 5c relocation. Look for stale prose or test pins that would still expect items 4-11 inline, missing aggregate test coverage, or doc surfaces that should mention the new driver. Cite specific file paths and line ranges for any issues found, and follow the output-format rules from your outer wrapper exactly.
